title: Data Type Creation Challenge
instructions: Create four variables with the correct data types. Each variable has been started for you - replace the placeholders (???) with the correct type of data.
steps: Change `item_name` to hold a string (text) value - any text you want!
Change `stock_count` to hold an integer (whole number) value.
Change `item_price` to hold a float (decimal number) value.
Change `is_available` to hold a boolean (True or False) value.
starterCode:
# Step 1: Replace ??? with a string (text)
item_name = ???
print(f"Item Name Type: {type(item_name)}")

# Step 2: Replace ??? with an integer (whole number)
stock_count = ???
print(f"Stock Count Type: {type(stock_count)}")

# Step 3: Replace ??? with a float (decimal number)
item_price = ???
print(f"Item Price Type: {type(item_price)}")

# Step 4: Replace ??? with a boolean (True or False)
is_available = ???
print(f"Availability Type: {type(is_available)}")
solution:
# Step 1: Replace ??? with a string (text)
item_name = "Laptop"
print(f"Item Name Type: {type(item_name)}")

# Step 2: Replace ??? with an integer (whole number)
stock_count = 150
print(f"Stock Count Type: {type(stock_count)}")

# Step 3: Replace ??? with a float (decimal number)
item_price = 12.99
print(f"Item Price Type: {type(item_price)}")

# Step 4: Replace ??? with a boolean (True or False)
is_available = True
print(f"Availability Type: {type(is_available)}")
hints: Strings need quotation marks around them (single or double).
Integers are whole numbers without decimal points.
Floats must include a decimal point, even if it's .0
Booleans must be capitalized: True or False (not true or false).
